sub: When to add or remove servers, with an ALB.

Overview.p: Scaling policies tell the ASG when to scale: target tracking, step, simple, scheduled or predictive. Health checks (EC2 or ELB) decide which instances to replace. With an ALB, use ELB health checks.
A thermostat for servers: keep average CPU near 50%. Add servers when hot, remove when cool. A doctor checks each server and replaces sick ones.
A shop keeps CPU near 50% with target tracking. When one server stops answering the ALB health check, the ASG replaces it.

items: CloudWatch collects a metric (CPU, request count)
A scaling policy compares it with the target
The ASG adds or removes instances
The ALB health check tests each target

items: Open your ASG > Automatic scaling > Create policy
Choose Target tracking, metric Average CPU, target 50
Attach the ALB target group in Integrations
Switch Health checks to ELB and set grace period 300 s
Generate load on one instance (command below)
Watch the Activity tab for new instances
Add a Scheduled action to set Desired 4 at 9 AM

Practical.p: Terminate or delete everything you created after practice to avoid charges.

items: Cap Max size to limit cost
Use ELB health checks so app failures are caught
Keep the health check path simple and light (/health)

Examples.p: scale on ALB request count per target.
scheduled scale up at 9 AM, down at 7 PM.

code: aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy --auto-scaling-group-name web-asg --policy-name cpu50 --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling --target-tracking-configuration file://tt.json

CLI Commands.p: IDs like i-0abc123 and sg-0abc123 are examples. Replace them with your real IDs.

items: Target tracking. You pick a metric and a target value and AWS does the rest.
EC2 only checks the instance. ELB also checks that the app answers, so use ELB with a load balancer.
Time after launch before health checks start, so the app can boot.
For known patterns such as office hours or planned sales.
How do ASG and ALB work together?
The ASG registers new instances in the target group, the ALB sends traffic once they are healthy and removes ones that fail.
